bible_refs.note: κοίτην ἔχουσα Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν completes the lemma begun at the end of u08-open; the full lemma is repeated later in the row.
Lemma: Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; μὴ ἀδικία παρὰ τῷ θεῷ; μὴ γένοιτο — exact, followed by κ.τ.λ.
ἕως καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς οὐ μόνον ἐξ Ἰουδαίων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν marks the end of the lemma range 9:14–24 (Paul: οὓς καὶ ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς).
ἠγαπῆσθαι … μεμισῆσθαι restates Τὸν Ἰακὼβ ἠγάπησα, τὸν δὲ Ἠσαῦ ἐμίσησα (Romans 9:13, from Malachi 1:2–3).
πρίν τι δράσαι τὰ βρέφη echoes μήπω γὰρ γεννηθέντων μηδὲ πραξάντων τι (9:11); εἰς δοῦλον τῷ ἐλάσσονι echoes ὁ μείζων δουλεύσει τῷ ἐλάσσονι (9:12, from Genesis 25:23).

choices.why: ῥοπῆς θελημάτων ἀβασανίστου: 'an untested leaning of wills', i.e. a choice made without any weighing of merit; rendered 'an untested swing of will'. ἰδίᾳ χάριτι κατανεύοντος τοῦ Θεοῦ: 'God nodding assent out of personal favour', i.e. favouritism, which the objectors allege.
σκαιός: literally 'left-handed', hence 'awkward, perverse'; set against σοφός ('wise').
προανατυποῦσθαι: 'to be prefigured, outlined beforehand'; rendered 'sketched out beforehand'.
ἀριστοτέχνας: 'supreme craftsman', an epithet of God as maker; kept.

pass_a_gloss: …having bed (κοίτην, conception) of Isaac our father. One must know that the aim (σκοπός) of the saying has in no way been concluded (συμπεπέρασται), but rather hangs (ἀπήρτηται), and needs some brief adding-on (ἐπαγωγῆς), that is, of things understood-in-addition (προσυπακουομένων), so that it not be seen limping (σκάζων). What I say is such: he showed beforehand, as from Isaac's having been given to Abraham from promise, that not by all means the children of the flesh, these would be counted to him also as seed, but it would befit him to be styled (χρηματίζειν) father of those from faith and promise; then he receives Rebecca and the things that happened in her case, and says 'And not only,' that is, not as far as the birth (γεννήσεως) of Isaac alone will my word arrive, 'but also Rebecca having bed from one, Isaac our father'; and it was necessary to bring on in addition: 'will be taken along perhaps for proof (ἀπόδειξιν) and full-assurance (πληροφορίαν),' that is, 'will be for outline (ὑποτύπωσιν) and image-making (εἰκονισμόν) of the calling (κλήσεως) and grace according to election (ἐκλογήν) and foreknowledge (πρόγνωσιν)'; for such a thing having been brought on, the saying would then have seemed to him just now completed; but I do not know how, passing this by, he has gone at once to the things said and done at the birth (γενέσει) of those from Isaac. 'What then shall we say? Not injustice (ἀδικία) with God? May it not be,' etc., until 'and called us not only from Jews but also from nations.' Since it was likely that some of the blame-lovers (φιλεγκλημόνων) would think Jacob and Esau to have met with an untested (ἀβασανίστου) inclination (ῥοπῆς) of wills (θελημάτων), and the one to have been loved by God nodding-assent (κατανεύοντος) with private grace (ἰδίᾳ χάριτι), the other to have been hated, the apostle necessarily removing beforehand (προαναιρῶν) as ruinous (ὀλέθριον) the assumption (διάληψιν) on this, tries to advocate (συνηγορεῖν) for the votes (ψήφοις) from above, setting up against his own words as it were the thing seeming to oppose; for if indeed, he says, even before the babes did anything and before trial itself and deeds, the one was deemed worthy of love, the other has been hated, and was ordered also as slave to the lesser, perhaps, he says, God is also unjust (ἄδικος); then how is this not stricken-senseless (ἀπόπληκτον)? For if Jacob had not become a good man, if Esau not wicked, someone would fittingly say that the foreknowledge perhaps had erred (πεπλανῆσθαι), and the things defined (ὡρισμένα) about both had become the work of a random (εἰκαίας) inclination and wills not secure (ἀσφαλῶν); but since Esau was very left-handed/perverse (σκαιός), and Jacob wise (σοφός), the foreknowledge of God would wrong nothing at all, granting even before the time to the one good in ways (τρόπους) to need to be loved, and to the one not such to be condemned (κατακρίνεσθαι); for for God to bear evil patiently (ἀνεξικακῆσαι) and to wait for the time of the deeds is nothing hard, so that from the deeds each might show through. But since it was necessary for the mystery (μυστήριον) of the grace according to election and of the gift (δωρεᾶς) in foreknowledge to be pre-typed (προανατυποῦσθαι), for this reason usefully God, the best-craftsman (ἀριστοτέχνας) of such things for us, all but even grasped (ἐπεδράττετο) the season, and in the birth of the children fully assured (πεπληροφόρηκε) Isaac that, being one and only from Abraham, he will be father of innumerable nations, those from promise and as to be called in faith; but if indeed according to…
pass_b_english: One should note that the aim of this sentence is by no means brought to completion; rather it is left hanging and needs a brief addition, that is, words to be understood, so that it may not appear to limp.

He had already shown, from the fact that Isaac was given to Abraham by promise, that the children of the flesh would not necessarily be counted to him as offspring, and that it would rather befit him to bear the name of father of those who are of faith and promise.

Then he takes up Rebecca and what happened in her case, and says, “And not only so,” that is, my argument will not stop at the birth of Isaac alone, “but also Rebecca, having conceived by one, our father Isaac” (Romans 9:10).

And he needed to add something like this: “will also be brought in as proof and assurance,” that is, “will serve as a pattern and image of the calling and grace that come by election and foreknowledge.”
For had something of that kind been added, his sentence would then have seemed complete.
But I do not know how he came to pass this over and go straight on to what was said and done at the birth of Isaac’s sons.
“What then shall we say? Is there injustice with God? By no means” (Romans 9:14), and so on, down to “he called us, not from the Jews only but also from the Gentiles” (Romans 9:24).

It was likely that some fault-finders would suppose that Jacob and Esau had met with an untested swing of will, and that the one was loved because God nodded assent out of personal favour, while the other was hated (Romans 9:13).

So the apostle of necessity does away in advance with this view of the matter as ruinous, and tries to speak in defence of the decrees from above, setting against his own words, as it were, what seems to oppose them.

For if, he says, even before the infants had done anything, before any testing of them and before any deeds, the one was thought worthy of love and the other was hated, and was even appointed to serve the younger (Romans 9:11–12), then perhaps, he says, God is even unjust.
And then how is this not senseless?

For if Jacob had not become a good man, if Esau had not been wicked, one might reasonably say that the foreknowledge had perhaps gone astray, and that what was determined for both of them was the work of a random impulse and an unsteady will.

But since Esau was very perverse and Jacob wise, God’s foreknowledge would do no wrong at all in granting, even ahead of time, to the one who was good in his ways that he should be loved, and to the one who was not such that he should be condemned.
For it would have been no hard thing for God to bear with them patiently and wait for the time of their deeds, so that each might be shown plainly by his own actions.

But since the mystery of grace by election and of the gift given in foreknowledge had to be sketched out beforehand, for that very reason God, our supreme craftsman in such things, put the moment to good use and all but seized it.

At the birth of the children he assured Isaac that, though he was the one and only son from Abraham, he would be the father of countless nations, those who are of the promise and who would be called in faith.

κοίτην ἔχουσα Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν. Ἰστέον ὅτι συμπεπέρασται μὲν οὐδαμῶς ὁ τοῦ
λόγου σκοπὸς, ἀπήρτηται δὲ μᾶλλον, καὶ δεῖταί τινος βραχείας ἐπαγωγῆς, ἤγουν
προσυπακουομένων, ἵνα μὴ σκάζων ὁρῶτο. ἔστι δὲ ὅ φημι τοιοῦτον· προαπέδειξε μὲν
γὰρ ὡς ἀπὸ τοῦ δεδόσθαι τῷ Ἁβραὰμ ἐξ ἐπαγγελίας τὸν Ἰσαὰκ, ὅτι μὴ πάντως τὰ τέκνα
τῆς σαρκὸς, ταῦτα αὐτῷ καταλογισθεῖεν ἂν καὶ εἰς σπέρμα, πρέποι δ' ἂν τὸ χρηματίζειν
αὐτὸν πατέρα τῶν ἐκ πίστεως καὶ ἐπαγγελίας· εἶτα δέχεται τὴν Ῥεβέκκαν καὶ τὰ ἐπ'
αὐτῇ γεγονότα, καί φησιν Οὐ μόνον δὲ, τουτέστιν οὐ μέχρι δὴ μόνης τῆς Ἰσαὰκ
γεννήσεως ὁ ἐμὸς ἀφίξεται λόγος, ἀλλὰ γὰρ καὶ Ῥεβέκκα ἐξ ἑνὸς κοίτην ἔχουσα Ἰσαὰκ
τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν· καὶ ἦν ἀναγκαῖον προσεπενεγκεῖν, συμπαραληφθήσεται τυχὸν πρὸς
ἀπόδειξιν καὶ πληροφορίαν, ἤγουν ἔσται πρὸς ὑποτύπωσιν καὶ εἰκονισμὸν τῆς κατ'

22

ἐκλογήν τε καὶ πρόγνωσιν κλήσεώς τε καὶ χάριτος· ἐπενηνεγμένου γὰρ τοιούτου τινὸς,
ἔδοξεν ἂν τότε ἀρτίως αὐτῷ πεποιῆσθαι λοιπὸν ὁ λόγος· ἀλλ' οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως τοῦτο
παρεὶς, ἐπ' αὐτὰ κεχώρηκεν εὐθὺς τὰ ἐπὶ τῇ γενέσει τῶν ἐξ Ἰσαὰκ εἰρημένα τε καὶ
πεπραγμένα. Τί οὖν ἐροῦμεν; μὴ ἀδικία παρὰ τῷ Θεῷ; μὴ γένοιτο κ.τ.λ. ἕως καὶ
ἐκάλεσεν ἡμᾶς οὐ μόνον ἐξ ἰουδαίων ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐξ ἐθνῶν. Ἐπειδὴ ἦν εἰκὸς τῶν
φιλεγκλημόνων οἴεσθαί τινας, ῥοπῆς 227 θελημάτων ἀβασανίστου τυχεῖν τὸν Ἰακὼβ
καὶ τὸν Ἡσαῦ, καὶ τὸν μὲν ἠγαπῆσθαι ἰδίᾳ χάριτι κατανεύοντος τοῦ Θεοῦ, τὸν δὲ
μεμισῆσθαι, προαναιρῶν ἀναγκαίως ὁ ἀπόστολος ὡς ὀλέθριον τὴν ἐπὶ τούτῳ διάληψιν,
ταῖς ἄνωθεν ψήφοις πειρᾶται συνηγορεῖν, τοῖς αὐτοῦ λόγοις τὸ ἀντιφέρεσθαι δοκοῦν
οἱονεί πως ἀντανιστάς· εἰ γὰρ δὴ, φησὶ, καὶ πρίν τι δράσαι τὰ βρέφη καὶ πρὸ πείρας
αὐτῆς καὶ πραγμάτων, ὁ μὲν τῆς ἀγάπης ἠξίωτο, ὁ δὲ μεμίσηται, τέτακτο δὲ καὶ εἰς
δοῦλον τῷ ἐλάσσονι, τάχα που, φησι, καὶ ἄδικος ὁ Θεός· εἶτα πῶς τοῦτο οὐκ
ἀπόπληκτον; εἰ μὲν γὰρ οὐ γέγονεν ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς ὁ Ἰακὼβ, εἰ μὴ πονηρὸς ὁ Ἡσαῦ, φαίη
τις ἂν εἰκότως πεπλανῆσθαι τάχα που τὴν πρόγνωσιν, καὶ ῥοπῆς εἰκαίας καὶ θελημάτων
οὐκ ἀσφαλῶν ἔργον γενέσθαι τὰ ἐπ' ἀμφοῖν ὡρισμένα· ἐπειδὴ δὲ σκαιὸς μὲν ἦν λίαν ὁ
Ἡσαῦ, σοφὸς δὲ ὁ Ἰακὼβ, ἀδικήσειεν ἂν ἡ τοῦ Θεοῦ πρόγνωσις τὸ σύμπαν οὐδὲν,
χαριζομένη καὶ πρὸ καιροῦ τῷ μὲν ἀγαθῷ τοὺς τρόπους τὸ ἀγαπᾶσθαι δεῖν, τῷ δὲ μὴ
τοιούτῳ τὸ κατακρίνεσθαι· ἀνεξικακῆσαι μὲν γὰρ τὸν Θεὸν, καὶ τὸν τῶν δρωμένων
περιμεῖναι καιρὸν χαλεπὸν οὐδὲν, ἵνα ἐξ αὐτῶν ἑκάτερος διαφαίνοιτο τῶν πραγμάτων.
ἐπειδὴ δὲ ἦν ἀναγκαῖον τῆς κατ' ἐκλογὴν χάριτος καὶ τῆς ἐν προγνώσει δωρεᾶς
προανατυποῦσθαι τὸ μυστήριον, ταύτῃτοι χρησίμως ὁ τῶν τοιούτων ἡμῖν ἀριστοτέχνας
Θεὸς, μονονουχὶ καὶ ἐπεδράττετο τοῦ καιροῦ, καὶ ἐν τῇ τῶν παίδων γενέσει
πεπληροφόρηκε τὸν Ἰσαὰκ, ὡς εἷς τε καὶ μόνος ὑπάρχων ἐξ Ἁβραὰμ, ἀναριθμήτων
ἔσται πατὴρ ἐθνῶν τῶν ἐξ ἐπαγγελίας καὶ ὡς ἐν πίστει κληθησομένων· εἰ δὲ δὴ κατὰ

review_notes: Staged row fixed in tr7.json. Unclear rendering of ῥοπῆς θελημάτων ἀβασανίστου ('a leaning of the will that weighed nothing beforehand') replaced with 'an untested swing of will'; ἰδίᾳ χάριτι κατανεύοντος τοῦ Θεοῦ now keeps God's nod ('God nodded assent out of personal favour'). 'somehow, I do not know how' doubled οὐκ οἶδα ὅπως; now said once. τάχα που … καὶ ἄδικος is 'even unjust', not 'unjust as well'. 'fully made' (calque of πεποιῆσθαι) now 'complete'. θελημάτων οὐκ ἀσφαλῶν is 'an unsteady will', not 'unsure choices'. Stiff 'called as in faith' smoothed to 'called in faith'. Translator note updated to match.
Copy-text: PG 74; Fragmenta in Romanos via Khazarzar (Fragmenta in sancti Pauli epistulam ad Romanos.pdf), PG columns 226–227.
The row opens inside the Romans 9:10 lemma that u08-open cut at ἐξ ἑνός; the English supplies 'having conceived by our father Isaac' from κοίτην ἔχουσα Ἰσαὰκ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν only.
The row ends mid-sentence at εἰ δὲ δὴ κατὰ; the object γνῶσιν heads u08-rem-mid. The English keeps the cut ('But if, in keeping with…') and adds nothing.
Inline page number 22 and PG column 227 are print markers and are left out of the English.

Cyril's grammatical remark: Paul's 'not only so, but also Rebecca …' (Romans 9:10) lacks a main verb. Cyril supplies the kind of words that would complete it, and they are given in quotation marks as his own suggestion, not as Scripture.

ῥοπῆς θελημάτων ἀβασανίστου: 'an untested leaning of wills', i.e. a choice made without any weighing of merit; rendered 'an untested swing of will'. ἰδίᾳ χάριτι κατανεύοντος τοῦ Θεοῦ: 'God nodding assent out of personal favour', i.e. favouritism, which the objectors allege.

The sentence 'For if, he says, even before the infants … God is unjust as well' voices the objection Paul raises against himself; Cyril then calls it senseless (ἀπόπληκτον). The voices are kept distinct: the objection is not Cyril's view.
σκαιός: literally 'left-handed', hence 'awkward, perverse'; set against σοφός ('wise').
προανατυποῦσθαι: 'to be prefigured, outlined beforehand'; rendered 'sketched out beforehand'.
ἀριστοτέχνας: 'supreme craftsman', an epithet of God as maker; kept.
ὡς ἐν πίστει κληθησομένων: 'as those to be called in faith'; rendered 'who would be called in faith'.
